reason: M3 is a diode-connected PMOS load on VOUT1; removing it still leaves VOUT1 pulled up via M5 (PMOS biased by VB1), so the output node won’t float. Caveat: without M3, the output’s DC bias point, output resistance, and gain may shift and VOUT1/VOUT2 symmetry may worsen unless the corresponding element on the other side is treated similarly.
impact_estimate: Low to moderate (mainly affects biasing/gain/symmetry, not basic operation).

reason: M4 is the analogous diode-connected PMOS load on VOUT2; VOUT2 can still be pulled up through M6 (VB1-biased PMOS). Caveat: removing only M4 (and not M3) can introduce offset/asymmetry; removing both M3 and M4 together is less disruptive than removing just one.
impact_estimate: Low to moderate (bias/gain/symmetry changes; basic amplification still possible).

reason: M6 is a PMOS current-source/pull-up controlled by VB1 for the VOUT2 branch; if M4 remains, VOUT2 still has a diode-connected pull-up path to VDD and the stage can still function as a (less ideal) differential pair. Caveat: output swing, gain, and bias current distribution change; for best symmetry you’d typically remove the matching device M5 as well or keep both.
impact_estimate: Moderate (noticeable load/bias change, but circuit still operates in a simplified form).
